label: Figure 30.1: Examples of poverty cycles
alt: Two circular poverty-cycle diagrams: a growth cycle linking low investment, low economic growth, low incomes and low savings, and a development cycle linking low incomes, low productivity, low human capital and low education/health care.
caption: Two self-reinforcing poverty cycles. In the growth cycle (left), low investment causes low economic growth, which causes low incomes, which causes low savings (a high marginal propensity to consume), which leaves too little available for investment – the cycle repeats. In the development cycle (right), low incomes cause low productivity, which causes low levels of human capital, which causes low levels of education and health care, which keeps incomes low – the cycle repeats. Breaking either loop at any point can help escape the poverty trap.
